findings.title: New install-declaration tests only exercise node removal
findings.fact: test_dropped_folder_filename_and_language_declarations_are_refused and test_existing_zip_receipt_also_rejects_undeclared_member cover dropping/removing a declared folder, filename, or language entry, but no test exercises attribute tampering (e.g. altering the 'plugin' attribute on the services folder) or reordering the files/languages children. The strict ordered-list equality in bgm_validate_install_declarations would reject both by inspection, but this is unverified by the test suite.
findings.recommendation: Optional: add one subtest that mutates an attribute or swaps the order of two folder/filename entries to pin the exact-match behavior, since the current tests only prove the removal path.

findings.title: REPAIR-CONTEXT.txt commits review-session narrative into tracked source history
findings.fact: The new REPAIR-CONTEXT.txt file embeds free-text adjudication conclusions, a review-session identifier, and asset checksums as a permanent repository file rather than as a commit message or PR description; the text also has irregular word-spacing (e.g. 'dropped3folders/3filenames/2languages', 'now explicit0644 beforeatomicreplace') suggesting it was pasted from another tool without cleanup.
findings.recommendation: Treat the file's claims (checksums, 'already proven' statements) as unverified assertions rather than evidence, since they are independently unenforced; consider moving this narrative to the commit message/PR description instead of a tracked file if it is not meant to be permanent project documentation.

scope: Narrow correction patch against previously reviewed complete distribution source. Review context existed only in private synthetic review fixture, not canonical project.

adjudication.basis: Strict attribute/order handling is enforced directly, independently inspected, and current native installs/package identity pass. Existing negative tests exercise the demonstrated missing-install-declaration failure boundary.

REPAIR-CONTEXT.txt is review input in a private synthetic Git fixture only. It is not tracked in the canonical repository. All substantive assertions were separately checked; no narrative is treated as provider/runtime evidence.

controllerJudgement: No remaining demonstrated release-tooling blocker; preserve the two minor observations without claiming a zero-findings review.
